html:
Franz Kafka was a German speaking Jewish writer, born in 1883 in Prague, whose stories of people trapped in senseless systems made him one of the most influential writers of the twentieth century.

He studied law and worked by day at an insurance institute for workers' accidents, writing at night. In The Metamorphosis of 1915 a salesman wakes up as a huge insect. In The Trial a man is arrested and condemned without ever learning the charge, and The Castle shows endless bureaucracy. He published little and asked his friend Max Brod to burn his papers; Brod published them instead. He died of tuberculosis in 1924. His three sisters were later murdered in the Holocaust. The word Kafkaesque came from his work, and he is a symbol of Prague's mixed Czech, German and Jewish past in Austria-Hungary.
sum: Franz Kafka was a German speaking Jewish writer, born in 1883 in Prague, whose stories of people trapped in senseless systems made him one of the most influential writers of the twentieth century.
